subtitulo: An opinion on learning with a reason and a limit
descripcion: At C1 the problem is no longer *how* to say what you think but how to say it so that it holds. A C1 opinion has three parts a B1 opinion doesn't: a stated position, a reason that isn't a restatement of the position, and an acknowledged limit. Most learners produce the first, skip the second and never reach the third — which is why their opinions sound firm but empty. The other half of the skill is eliciting: pulling a real opinion out of someone who is being polite or vague.

filas: *I'd say* → *My sense is* → *My position is* → *I'd argue*
supplies the reason, not a restatement
*because* → *the reason being* → *what makes me say that is*
splits a question others treat as one
*I'd separate two things* / *I'd distinguish between X and Y*
*Where I'd stop short is* / *I wouldn't extend it to*
That's my instinct, not my evidence
*What's your read?* → *Where do you land?* → *Is that a hunch or have you seen it?*
*You'd know better than me* / *I'm outside my lane*

ejemplos.texto: *My position is that hybrid work only fails where management was already weak — the office was covering for the problem, not solving it.*
*I'd distinguish between two things: whether it works, and whether people like it.*
*Where I'd stop short is claiming this applies to every role.*
*Is that a hunch, or have you actually seen it happen?*

notas: *I think* isn't weak, but it's cheap. Rotate through the framing column instead of repeating it.
*I'd distinguish between X and Y* is the highest-value move here: it signals you've thought about the question rather than reacted to it.
Naming the limit of your own claim strengthens it. Counter-intuitive, but reliably true in English argument.

es.en: Spanish can hedge inside the verb (*creo que sea* vs. *creo que es*); English can't. *I think* is only a frame, never a hedge, so English needs a second device stacked on top of it to soften anything.
es.es: El español puede atenuar dentro del verbo («creo que sea» frente a «creo que es»); el inglés no puede. «I think» es solo un marco, no un atenuante, por lo que el inglés necesita un segundo recurso encima de él para suavizar una afirmación.

de.en: German softens with the Konjunktiv II and particles (das wäre wohl…, ich würde sagen), and would and I'd say are good English equivalents. The particles themselves have no counterpart, so German speakers need an extra lexical hedge in English (probably, a bit).
de.de: Deutsch schwächt mit Konjunktiv II und Partikeln ab («das wäre wohl…», «ich würde sagen»), und «would» bzw. «I'd say» sind gute englische Entsprechungen. Die Partikeln selbst haben keine direkte Entsprechung, daher brauchen Deutschsprachige im Englischen oft eine zusätzliche lexikalische Abschwächung wie «probably» oder «a bit».

it.en: Italian, like Spanish, can hedge inside the verb (penso che sia rather than è; sarebbe), which English cannot do. I think is only a frame in English, so Italian speakers need a second device (probably, might) to soften a claim.
it.it: L'italiano, come lo spagnolo, può attenuare dentro il verbo («penso che sia» invece di «è»; «sarebbe»), cosa che l'inglese non può fare. «I think» è solo una cornice in inglese, quindi serve un secondo dispositivo («probably», «might») per attenuare l'affermazione.

fr.en: French softens with the conditionnel (ce serait plutôt…), which maps well onto English would. After je pense que French uses the indicative, as English does, so French speakers mainly need to add lexical hedges (probably, a bit).
fr.fr: Le français atténue avec le conditionnel («ce serait plutôt…»), qui se rend bien par «would». Après «je pense que», le français utilise l'indicatif comme l'anglais ; il faut surtout ajouter des hedges lexicaux comme «probably» ou «a bit».

pt.en: Portuguese can hedge inside the verb with the subjunctive (não acho que seja), which English cannot do. I think is only a frame in English, so Portuguese speakers need a second device (probably, might) to soften a claim.
pt.pt: O português pode atenuar dentro do verbo com o subjuntivo («não acho que seja»), algo que o inglês não pode fazer. «I think» é apenas uma moldura em inglês, então falantes de português precisam de um segundo recurso («probably», «might») para suavizar uma afirmação.

errores: Circular reasoning: *I think remote work is good because working remotely is beneficial.*
*In my humble opinion* — reads as sarcastic to native ears. Avoid entirely.
*According to me* — not English. Use *in my view*.
Over-reliance on *for me*, which frames a judgement as a mere preference.

es: *Sinceramente* as an opener rendered as *Sincerely,* instead of *Honestly* or *Frankly*.
de: *Ehrlich gesagt* rendered as *Honestly said* instead of *To be honest*.
it: *Sinceramente* as an opener rendered as *Sincerely,* instead of *Honestly* or *Frankly*.
fr: *Je trouve que* rendered as *I find that* in every judgement instead of *I think* or *My sense is*.
pt: *Sinceramente* as an opener rendered as *Sincerely,* instead of *Honestly* or *Frankly*.

mision.consigna: Give your honest view on whether employers should pay for *continuing education* that doesn't relate to the job.
requisitos: a stated position, a reason that isn't a restatement, and an acknowledged limit
one question that invites the other person's view
use *career path*, *continuing education* and *to keep up to date*

microtareas.texto: Write your opinion on *continuing education* in one line. Underneath, the reason. Underneath, where you'd stop short.
Ask someone *Where do you land on…?* about *on-the-job training* at work. Write down their answer.
Record 90 seconds: *Is a degree still the best start to a career path?* End with a limit.

autochequeo: Is my reason different from my position, or just a restatement?
Did I name one limit of my own claim?
Three different framing expressions, or *I think* three times?
Is my distinction a real distinction, or two words for the same thing?
All four core items — count them.
promptCorreccion: Focus only on how I express opinions. (1) Mark each framing device and say if it fits the register. (2) Point out any circular reasoning. (3) Is my distinction real or just two words for the same thing? (4) Rewrite my three weakest sentences. Do not rewrite the whole text — I want to see my own errors.
